summary: Every piece is built around a person who looks very closely at a small world without stepping into it. Simone Weil called attention the rarest and purest form of generosity, and all four writers treat watching as a moral act as much as a sensory one. It is also the first lesson of the year: before voice and structure, a writer has to learn to look.

pieces.essay: Woolf at her window gives a dying insect her whole attention, and that attention is what turns it into a story about life and death.
pieces.poem: Oliver kneels in the grass with a grasshopper and says outright that she doesn't know how to pray, only how to pay attention.
pieces.story: Miss Brill watches everyone in the park and narrates their lives; the story turns when she discovers what it's like to be watched back.
pieces.song: Ray Davies' narrator stays at his window watching Terry and Julie cross the river, and says he doesn't need friends as long as he can watch the sunset.

forYou: Jasmine in When Jasmine Blooms starts as a watcher: something arrives (a melody) and she can't stop attending to it. Miss Brill's turn, the watcher suddenly being watched, is a useful shape for the moment Melur looks back at her.
